description: Generic administrative and organisational controls that apply across multiple mechanisms. These are the managed layer — human-dependent, lower reliability than engineered controls, but universally applicable.

mitigations.name: risk_assessment
mitigations.description: Task-specific risk assessment or method statement (RAMS) identifying hazards and specifying controls. Does not physically mitigate — ensures other controls are identified and planned.
mitigations.pfd_source: LOPA: PFD 0.15 for administrative controls. Failure: generic/copy-paste assessment, not task-specific, not read by workers, controls identified but not implemented.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Effectiveness is entirely indirect — the value is in identifying and specifying the controls. A risk assessment that sits in a folder is worthless.

mitigations.name: competent_person
mitigations.description: Trained, experienced person supervising the work. Can identify changing conditions, enforce controls, stop work. The human element of the safety system.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.15. Failure: person not actually competent (has the title but not the knowledge), not present during critical phases, production pressure overrides safety judgement.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: A genuinely competent supervisor catches the things that procedures miss — changing conditions, shortcuts, complacency. Effectiveness varies hugely with the individual.

mitigations.name: training_awareness
mitigations.description: Hazard-specific training and toolbox talks. Builds awareness but does not physically prevent the event. Knowledge decays without reinforcement.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.20. Failure: training not retained (Ebbinghaus curve — 70% forgotten within 24 hours without reinforcement), not specific to the task, language/literacy barriers.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Training alone has low effectiveness — knowledge doesn't equal behaviour. Most effective when combined with practical reinforcement and competent supervision.

mitigations.name: stop_work_authority
mitigations.description: Any worker can stop work if they perceive unsafe conditions. Cultural control — only works if the organisation genuinely supports it without reprisal.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.30. High PFD because exercising stop work requires psychological safety. Failure: worker doesn't speak up (fear of reprisal, peer pressure, production pressure), concern dismissed by supervisor.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When exercised and respected, stops the event before it occurs. The most powerful managed control — but also the most culturally dependent. Organisations with high Voice scores (cultural graph) have more effective stop work authority.

mitigations.name: emergency_plan
mitigations.description: Documented emergency plan with trained first aiders, communication protocol, evacuation routes, external service liaison. Framework for post-impact response.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.15. Failure: plan not rehearsed, first aiders not available (shift coverage), communication breakdown, external services delayed.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Reduces response time and ensures appropriate first aid. Effectiveness depends on rehearsal frequency and personnel availability.

mitigations.name: first_aid
mitigations.description: Workplace first aiders with appropriate equipment (AED, burns kit, trauma kit). Provides immediate treatment before ambulance. AED within 3 min is the highest-impact first aid intervention.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.15. Failure: first aider not on shift, equipment not maintained (AED battery, expired supplies), first aider panics or doesn't respond.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: AED within 3 min: ~70% survival from VF cardiac arrest vs ~5% without. Burns: immediate cooling reduces severity. Trauma: bleeding control saves lives. Effectiveness is intervention-specific.
